tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the tape's disagreement now the loudest in the table and the row named as the likeliest source of the tilt scorecard's negative spread. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: C now, D prior at the industry, with Hotels A, Online retail A, Physical retail B and Apparel B: the market is buying the European consumer. The reasons that set F (United States consumer surveys falling, the European consumer never read, a regime that sells discretionary spend) could not be re-tested: no consumer survey for any G10 country was in window this week. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Held because nothing on the causes side changed and a move on the tape alone against two unread legs would be a moved goalpost; the exceptions stay at sector level (Physical retail C). Counter-case: a double notch on 138 stocks against four sectors at A or B on relative strength shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists for the industry where cheap good businesses accumulate, and eight weeks of negative tilt spreads are consistent with this row being wrong. To D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or a second industry reading at C or better with Hotels and Online retail holding A.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged, with the fuel leg stronger. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 is the airlines' largest cost, the US consumer surveys fell again, and no source spoke to airlines. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: F now, F prior. Held D, not F, because no Pool name sits here and the new evidence is a price, not a read on the group. Counter-case: capacity discipline and fourteen stocks already derated.

geography.why: Overweight, carried; the condition (back to C if Brent falls under $85 or Oslo's leadership reverses for four weeks) could not be tested: no Brent level reached the pack, the only oil read is an undated headline that oil is dipping on peace hopes, and Oslo was not read. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Energy relative strength slipped to B from A at the industry with Upstream still A. Counter-case: this double counts the Energy rows for most of the 46 Norwegian stocks, and a Ukraine ceasefire takes the premium out of crude. Back to C if Brent is read under $85.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
